title: See Israel's Gentle Shepherd Stand
description: See Israel's Gentle Shepherd Stand in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 445, “Suffer Little Children to Come unto Me”, where the book credits them to Flint's Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: See Is-rael's gen-tle Shep-herd stand With all en-gag-ing charms! Hark, how he calls the ten-der lambs, And folds them in his arms!

lines: Hark, how he calls the tender lambs,
And folds them in his arms!
Of such is heaven; and souls like these
Shall find in heaven their home."
We bring them, Lord, with thankful hands,
And yield them up to Thee;
Joyful that we ourselves are Thine,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
